title: BTC Universe
subtitle: Protocol, network, mining, custody and Lightning payment layers
disclaimer: A sourced Bitcoin ecosystem map. It is technical/research context, not investment advice or a price forecast.

nodes.label: Bitcoin
nodes.description: Peer-to-peer electronic cash system and monetary network described in the Bitcoin white paper.

nodes.label: Blockchain
nodes.description: Ordered, timestamped public ledger of validated blocks maintained independently by full nodes.

nodes.label: Blocks
nodes.description: Containers for validated transactions linked by previous-block hashes.

nodes.label: Transactions
nodes.description: Signed transfers that spend previous transaction outputs and create new outputs.

nodes.label: UTXO Set
nodes.description: Unspent transaction outputs form Bitcoin's spendable state model.

nodes.label: Transaction Fees
nodes.description: Fees compensate miners for including transactions and vary with block-space demand.

nodes.label: Full Nodes
nodes.description: Nodes independently validate blocks and transactions against consensus rules.

nodes.label: P2P Network
nodes.description: Peer-to-peer relay layer used to propagate transactions and blocks.

nodes.label: Consensus Rules
nodes.description: Validation rules that full nodes enforce when accepting blocks and transactions.

nodes.label: Wallets
nodes.description: Software that manages keys, receives bitcoin and constructs/signs spending transactions.

nodes.label: Keys & Signatures
nodes.description: Private keys authorize spends; public keys/signatures let the network verify authorization.

nodes.label: Self-Custody
nodes.description: Users control the private keys required to spend their bitcoin.

nodes.label: Hosted Custody
nodes.description: Third-party services hold private keys on behalf of users; operational and counterparty risks differ from self-custody.

nodes.label: Mining
nodes.description: Process that adds new blocks and makes modification of transaction history computationally difficult.

nodes.label: Proof of Work
nodes.description: Computational work used in block production and chain-selection security.

nodes.label: Miners / Pools
nodes.description: Solo miners and pools compete to produce valid blocks and receive block rewards plus fees.

nodes.label: Lightning Network
nodes.description: Peer-to-peer payment network using channels anchored to Bitcoin for low-cost, near-instant bitcoin payments.

nodes.label: Payment Channels
nodes.description: Bilateral channels that anchor to the Bitcoin blockchain and support off-chain updates.

nodes.label: Lightning Routing
nodes.description: Payments can traverse a route of Lightning nodes and channels to reach a recipient.

nodes.label: Lightning Invoices
nodes.description: Recipient-generated payment requests describing amount and routing/payment information.

nodes.label: Fiat ↔ BTC Bridges
nodes.description: Regulated exchanges, brokers and payment services connect Bitcoin with fiat-denominated financial systems.

nodes.label: Market Price
nodes.description: Exchange prices are external market signals and are not consensus data from the Bitcoin protocol.

nodes.label: Security Model
nodes.description: Security emerges from independent validation, cryptographic authorization, proof of work and operational key protection.
